column1: # Game profile of Road 96 (Switch, update v327680 = 1.05 on the base game v0). Plays on the Mac
# Unity IL2CPP on SDK 11.4.3, NVN, FMOD (sound through AudioOut), VP8 movies through NintendoSDK_movie (subsdk0). The survey finds the strings of Unity 2019.3.0f5 and 2020.3.12f1.
# Shaders: from the UnityFS bundles under Data/ (shader_split.py) and Unity's 11 GLSLC outputs in main
# subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie, which main imports from
# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource (virtual address memory). At startup the game takes pool − used as one 3.14 GB address region, and Unity maps its allocators beside it.
# The NSP script's heap check (alias region used up to +4.27 GB of 4.38 GB, no heap set) wrote a 1 GB pool and kept Engage's 5 GB block (4.375 GB alias region). Both were wrong here:

#   - 1 GB pool: the game's allocator ran out at 1.5 GB mapped, 10 s into the title, and an unchecked NULL from its block allocator (main+0x225ef4, a memset of 0x368 bytes at sdk+0x53b41c) crashed it.
#   - 3285 MB pool (the Switch's, the survey's value) in the 4.375 GB alias region: the region was full at startup (+4.25 GB), and the next address reservation returned 0 about 30 s in
#     (main+0x924c18, Unity's virtual block allocator writing through the NULL it got).

# With a 3285 MB pool and a 7 GB block (6.375 GB alias region) the title ran 3,300 frames (110 s) with no red line and a flat 30 fps; the alias region's high-water mark was +4.76 GB, past the old 4.375 GB.
# Not measured: the iPhone, and play beyond the title screens

# the NVN depth mode the game sets (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode near = 0): the pipeline archive made offline holds the main0_z vertex entries (dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py). Without this key the bundled archive was built for near = -w and the
# host skipped it ("the game's depth mode is not the one built for"), so every pipeline was built when first drawn: hitches of 0.1–1.8 s at each new scene
